solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman gathers information for things to be done

indicators.note: a woman gathering something holds it within her, so her name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A woman collects the facts she needs before drawing up her to-do list.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting is a direct synonym for the business to be done.

clue.text: Dire Straits are recording ones

indicators.note: dire means dreadful or in a bad state, so these letters are put into a bad order

explanation.surface: A remark that the rock band Dire Straits are performers who make records.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits looks like the band's name read whole, but 'Dire' is the anagram signal working on the word straits.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording ones are performers who make records, the people the music industry calls its signed acts.

clue.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

definitions.text: Return to the country, the scene of the crime

parts.words: Return to the country, the scene of the crime
parts.note: reads like a holiday trip home, but describes legally handing a suspect back to the nation where the offence took place

explanation.definitionFit: Formally handing over an accused person to the state where they allegedly offended is exactly this legal process.

clue.text: At high cost? Extremely

definitions.meaning: to pay for something this way is to pay a heavy price
as in loving someone very much

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb covers both a heavy price paid and a very great degree, as in loving someone deeply.

clue.text: Side passage for those taking flight?

parts.note: side is pretentious manner, as is putting on airs
a passage is a journey, a trip

explanation.surface: A side corridor set aside for people escaping in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' means swagger or pretension, as in 'putting on side', which matches AIRS; 'taking flight' suggests fleeing but means flying in aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is a facility built for aircraft and their passengers taking off and landing.

clue.text: Early centre of missionaries

indicators.note: the middle stretch of the word missionaries supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A note on where missionary work first spread from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' looks like part of the definition, a mission base, but 'centre of' also picks the middle of missionaries; St Columba's Hebridean island monastery was an early Christian base.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish island where Columba founded his monastery in 563 was an early Christian hub.

clue.text: Refuse to allow a seamstress time

parts.note: a seamstress is someone who sews
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to give a dressmaker any time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, waste matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste matter carried away by drains is the noun sense of refuse, rubbish or sewage.

clue.text: Concerning the first female mate of the ruff

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
in the Bible Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: A remark about the original woman and her partner, who wears a frilly collar.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruff is a wading bird, not an Elizabethan collar; its female has her own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithologists call the female of the ruff, a sandpiper, by this separate name.

clue.text: Take the lead, but quietly drop back later

indicators.note: later says the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to drop back is to recede

explanation.surface: Advice to a runner: go to the front, then ease off and fall behind afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To go before or in front of others is to lead, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: It returned more than once to an old master

indicators.note: more than once says the reversed piece is repeated
returned means the word It is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something keeps coming back to a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning IT gives TI, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian, the Venetian Renaissance painter, is a classic example of an Old Master.

clue.text: New Year when there's a situation of uncertainty

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over in a fresh form

explanation.surface: Someone notes that New Year's Eve brings an uncertain mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is at no particular place leaves its location undecided, an unfixed position.

clue.text: Hold on, I can't move!

indicators.note: move tells us to shift these letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to wait cries out that they are stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something within is to hold it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stop one on a horse

parts.note: to stall is to stop
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt a rider who is mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse is called this, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Be still shivering

parts.note: combines staying motionless with being so cold that one shivers

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to stop moving completely and to be very cold, both senses nudged here.

clue.text: One note noisy and two not clear

parts.note: C is a musical note
noisy means loud
two more notes, E and D

explanation.surface: A muddled musical description: a single loud tone and a pair that sound murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured by haze or confusion is not clear, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pole to feel sick on voyage

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: A Polish traveller gets seasick on a sea journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland, but it is the magnetic or geographic pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail can mean to make a voyage by sea, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A prison-camp child growing up

definitions.note: describes a cave deposit that builds upward, though the clue phrase is verbal

parts.note: a Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child raised in a wartime prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing up' seems to be about the child but describes a cave formation that rises from the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral column formed by drips builds upward from a cave floor, unlike its hanging partner.

clue.text: Delayed entering aisle, distressed, being nervous

indicators.note: entering puts one piece inside the other
distressed means damaged or disturbed, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: delayed means late

explanation.surface: A late passenger squeezing into a crowded aisle feels anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delayed' looks like the definition of a late passenger, but it supplies the inserted piece; 'distressed' only scrambles the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling uncomfortable and uneasy is the idiom's meaning, matching anxious.

clue.text: Poem completed but not written down

parts.note: something completed is past
oral means spoken, not written

explanation.surface: A verse composition finished but only ever recited.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem idealising rural life is called this, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Not having a steady position as croupier, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be put in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A casino worker's job is insecure.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstable and liable to fall describes something without firm footing.

clue.text: Two girls, one on each knee

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
Ella is another girl's name

explanation.surface: A pair of daughters, each sitting on a parent's knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap bone sits at the front of each knee joint, one per leg.

clue.text: Turn pale — guilty perhaps?

indicators.note: turn signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes white; might they have done it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'guilty perhaps' is an example: what a defendant says in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant's formal answer to a charge in court, of which guilty is one possible example.

clue.text: Feeling guilty, has made reparations

indicators.note: read as re-parations, the letters are parted and put back together

explanation.surface: Someone remorseful has paid compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame is the feeling of guilt or embarrassment over what one has done.

clue.text: A naval officer bearing one star

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
one's air is one's bearing or manner

explanation.surface: A naval officer wearing a single star on the uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila, so it is one particular star.

clue.text: Appeals for casual worker, a good man, to return

parts.note: a temp is a temporary or casual worker

indicators.note: to return says the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Job adverts appeal for a temporary worker, a decent person, to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal to someone is to attract or entice them, matching the verb.

clue.text: Imitate one in opera hitting a note

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Copy an opera singer as she reaches a high note.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone's manner or voice is a direct synonym.

clue.text: How to pedal to coast

parts.note: pressing the car's foot pedal to disengage the drive lets a vehicle freewheel

explanation.definitionFit: Releasing the engine from the gearbox with the clutch pedal lets a car roll freely.

clue.text: The first person to study a work of art

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to examine a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious painting on wood, often Orthodox, is an example of a work of art.

clue.text: Rice cooked with milk and port

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been fiddled or worked over

explanation.surface: A rice pudding recipe followed by a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the after-dinner drink but is the Irish city and harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Limerick is a port city on the River Shannon in Ireland, an example.

clue.text: Scholar regrettably rejected an Arab's greeting

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are sent back, read backwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A learned man sadly refused an Arab's welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A low bow with the right hand on the forehead is a traditional greeting in Arabic-speaking countries.

clue.text: Port reached with luck and a fortuitous break

indicators.note: a break breaks up the letters, as if by chance

explanation.surface: A ship arrives in harbour thanks to good fortune and a lucky chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Auckland is New Zealand's largest city and main port, an example.

clue.text: Supporter of half-day closing

indicators.note: half says only the first half of the weekday's name is kept

parts.note: closing means end

explanation.surface: Someone in favour of shops shutting for half the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'day' stands for the weekday name, of which only the front half is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally or backer is someone on your side, which this word can mean.
